title: Assessment of Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experiences: A Meeting Report
population: Researchers and practitioners in course-based undergraduate research at a national meeting; n not given
method_studied: Assessment of course-based undergraduate research experiences
finding: The meeting found no shared, validated instrument for assessing outcomes of course-based research; existing assessments were program-specific, self-report-based or borrowed.
notes: Meeting report. Raw pass adds the CURE model definition: discovery, broad relevance, collaboration, iteration.

title: How should the advancement of large language models affect the practice of science?
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
population: Four invited groups of scientists; no study sample
method_studied: How large language models should change scientific practice
finding: Four groups take four positions on LLM use in science and no single position is adopted; the field has not converged on governance or evaluation.
notes: Opinion piece.

title: Using Cognitive Psychology to Understand GPT-3
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
population: GPT-3 tested on cognitive psychology tasks; no human sample size given
method_studied: Cognitive-psychology test batteries applied to a language model
finding: GPT-3 matched or exceeded human performance on a multi-armed bandit task and showed errors on multi-step logical inference, with small phrasing changes swinging accuracy.
notes: Subject is a model, so the record bears on learners only by analogy.

title: Understanding Scientific Understanding
method_studied: Definition of scientific understanding through intelligible theories
finding: A scientist understands a phenomenon when they can build a qualitative explanation from an intelligible theory without the full calculation; intelligibility shifts historically with tools and training.
notes: Book. Supplies a criterion for understanding that a learning corpus can test against.

title: The Automation of Science
population: Robot scientist Adam working on yeast gene function
method_studied: Closed-loop automated hypothesis generation and experiment
finding: Adam generated hypotheses, ran the experiments and interpreted results with no human in the loop; some findings were independently confirmed as novel.
notes: Scope was one model organism and a bounded hypothesis space.

title: Nobel Turing Challenge: Creating the Engine for Scientific Discovery
method_studied: Grand challenge for autonomous AI discovery
finding: Proposes an AI system that hypothesizes, experiments and produces a Nobel-worthy discovery; autonomous experimentation is named as the binding constraint.
notes: Position paper.

title: On scientific understanding with artificial intelligence
population: None, perspective with a survey of approaches
method_studied: Criteria for when AI contributes to human scientific understanding
finding: Prediction accuracy alone does not count as understanding; a human must be able to internalize and independently apply the pattern the AI found.
notes: Surveys four categories of AI-for-understanding approaches.

title: Predicting research trends with semantic and neural networks with an application in quantum physics
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
population: Concept co-occurrence graph of quantum-physics papers
method_studied: Neural-network prediction of future research topics from a concept graph
finding: The model predicted which unstudied concept pairs would become active topics at accuracy above random and popularity baselines; physicists judged several suggestions plausible.
notes: Record gives no accuracy figure.

title: Toward systematic review automation: a practical guide to using machine learning tools in research synthesis
population: Survey of machine-learning tools for systematic reviews
method_studied: Machine assistance for screening and data extraction in evidence synthesis
finding: ML tools assist screening and extraction, and no tool fully automates synthesis and judgment; screening-ranking tools are the most validated.
notes: Practical guide.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Illusions of Understanding in Scientific Research
method_studied: Illusions of understanding produced by AI tools in research
finding: Researchers can accept an AI explanation as their own understanding without being able to reconstruct it, and AI tools can make a narrow slice of a space feel like the whole.
notes: Raw pass names four AI roles: oracle, surrogate, quant, arbiter.

title: Automating the practice of science: Opportunities, challenges, and implications
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Surveys the current scope of automation in science, separating opportunities from bottlenecks and from ethical consequences.
notes: Perspective and survey.

title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
population: 43 expert researchers, each executing one randomly assigned research idea over 100+ hours
method_studied: Executing LLM-generated versus human-written research ideas
finding: After execution and blind review, scores for LLM-generated ideas dropped more than scores for human ideas, and on several metrics human ideas ranked higher.
notes: arXiv preprint. Record gives no score values.

title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
population: 100+ expert NLP researchers as writers and blind reviewers
method_studied: LLM-generated versus human research ideas rated blind
finding: Experts rated LLM ideas as more novel than human ideas and not more feasible; LLM outputs showed less diversity.
notes: arXiv preprint, tier candidate. Appears twice in the raw passes.

title: ChatGPT listed as author on research papers: many scientists disapprove
method_studied: AI tools credited as authors on research papers
finding: Papers listing a generative AI tool as co-author drew objections, and publishers barred AI author credit while allowing disclosed assistive use.
notes: News article, tier candidate.

title: Scientific discovery in the age of artificial intelligence
population: Review of AI-for-science methods across fields
method_studied: AI across the stages of the discovery pipeline
finding: The most mature results sit in representation learning and prediction; generation and closed-loop autonomy are early, and evaluation is a weak point across the field.
notes: Narrative review.

title: Developing and Assessing a Force and Motion Learning Progression
population: Students placed on a five-level force and motion progression; n not given
method_studied: Validating a learning progression with interviews, ordered multiple choice and IRT
finding: Three placement methods agreed for only a modest majority of students, and some students appeared to skip an intermediate level.
notes: Record gives no agreement figure.

title: A Taxonomy for Learning, Teaching, and Assessing: A Revision of Bloom's Taxonomy of Educational Objectives
finding: Replaces Bloom's single dimension with six cognitive processes crossed against four knowledge types, with Create as the top process.
notes: Book verified by ISBN 978-0-8013-1903-7 in the record.

title: When and where do we apply what we learn?: A taxonomy for far transfer.
method_studied: Taxonomy of transfer distance along nine dimensions
finding: Most transfer research clusters at the near end; far-transfer effects are often small or null, and explicit instruction in transfer strategies helps more than content mastery alone.
notes: Review with taxonomy.

title: Origin and Description of the SOLO Taxonomy
venue: Evaluating the Quality of Learning: The SOLO Taxonomy (Structure of the Observed Learning Outcome), Academic Press
method_studied: SOLO taxonomy for coding the structure of a response
finding: A response is coded by structural complexity into five levels from prestructural to extended abstract, independent of correctness, and the level belongs to the response and changes task to task.
notes: Raw pass: descriptive taxonomy, no effect size.

title: The 2 Sigma Problem: The Search for Methods of Group Instruction as Effective as One-to-One Tutoring
population: Students in studies by Bloom's doctoral students; n not given in the record
method_studied: One-to-one tutoring with mastery learning versus conventional group instruction
finding: Tutoring plus mastery feedback moved the average student to the 98th percentile of the control group; mastery learning alone reached about one standard deviation.
effect: 2.0 SD for tutoring plus mastery learning; about 1.0 SD for mastery learning alone
notes: Tier outcome. Kulik 1990 in this corpus puts group mastery nearer 0.5 SD. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/sub-outcomes/education/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-ce3245fc58e7).

title: Rethinking Transfer: A Simple Proposal with Multiple Implications
method_studied: Preparation for future learning as a transfer measure
finding: Standard unassisted transfer tests undercount learning; a test that hands learners a new resource shows an advantage for learners who built generalizable structure.

title: Self-Explanations: How Students Study and Use Examples in Learning to Solve Problems
population: Students studying worked physics examples; n not given
finding: Students who generated more self-explanations solved later problems more correctly; quality of explanation mattered more than study time or example count.
notes: Raw pass: correlational comparison of high and low self-explainers.

title: Eliciting Self‐Explanations Improves Understanding
population: Students reading a science text, prompted versus unprompted; n not given
finding: Prompted students gained more from pretest to posttest than unprompted students, controlling for time on task; high explainers nearly all reached a correct mental model.
notes: Assignment procedure is not stated in the record.

title: The ICAP Framework: Linking Cognitive Engagement to Active Learning Outcomes
population: Review of studies across domains and ages
method_studied: ICAP ordering of engagement: interactive, constructive, active, passive
finding: Learning is predicted to rise from passive to active to constructive to interactive; evidence is clearest for the first two steps and thinner for interactive over constructive.
notes: Framework paper.

title: Knowledge tracing: Modeling the acquisition of procedural knowledge
population: Students using an intelligent tutor; n not given
method_studied: Bayesian knowledge tracing of skill mastery
finding: A four-parameter hidden-state model of mastery predicted individual learning curves and post-test performance better than a fixed-trials rule.
notes: Record year 1995; raw pass cites 1994 with DOI 10.1007/BF01099821. Model assumes no forgetting.

title: Learning Progressions in Science: An Evidence-Based Approach to Reform
venue: Consortium for Policy Research in Education Research Report #RR-63
finding: A progression stays a hypothesis until tested on learner data, can be valid for one curriculum only, and its assessment items need separate validation.
notes: CPRE report RR-63.

title: Intrinsic Motivation and the Process of Learning: Beneficial Effects of Contextualization, Personalization, and Choice
population: Elementary school children on computer arithmetic activities; n not given
finding: Each of the three raised motivation, depth of engagement, amount learned in a fixed time and perceived competence over an abstract control.
notes: Record reports large increases without a number.

title: A Meta-Analytic Review of Experiments Examining the Effects of Extrinsic Rewards on Intrinsic Motivation
population: Pooled experiments on rewards; count not given in the record
finding: Tangible, expected, performance-contingent rewards undermined intrinsic motivation; verbal praise raised it; unexpected rewards did not undermine.
notes: Record gives no pooled effect.

title: The "What" and "Why" of Goal Pursuits: Human Needs and the Self-Determination of Behavior
finding: Conditions that satisfy the three needs raise intrinsic motivation; extrinsic motivators differ by whether the goal is internalized.
notes: Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/curiosity-and-motivation/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-25a39cdf1218).

title: Financial Incentives and Student Achievement: Evidence from Randomized Trials
population: Students in randomized trials in more than one city; n not given in the record
method_studied: Paying students for outputs versus inputs
finding: Pay for test scores produced no significant gain in either city tested; pay for inputs such as books read produced gains in at least one of two cities.
notes: Record gives no effect size.

title: Pay Enough or Don't Pay at All
population: Experimental participants and daycare centers; n not given
finding: Small payments produced worse performance than no payment or a larger payment, and a small daycare fine raised late pickups.
notes: Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/curiosity-and-motivation/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-c74ae7c50c71).

title: Information-Seeking, Curiosity, and Attention: Computational and Neural Mechanisms
method_studied: Curiosity as intrinsic reward for expected information gain
finding: Attention and information-seeking target moderate, resolvable uncertainty; information-seeking and reward-seeking share circuitry.

title: States of Curiosity Modulate Hippocampus-Dependent Learning via the Dopaminergic Circuit
population: Participants in an fMRI trivia task; n not given
finding: High-curiosity answers were remembered better at a one-day delay, and curiosity raised memory for unrelated material shown while waiting.
notes: Within-subject lab study. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/curiosity-and-motivation/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-10b268b14f29).

title: An NCME Instructional Module on: Comparison of Classical Test Theory and Item Response Theory and Their Applications to Test Development
method_studied: Classical test theory versus item response theory
finding: Classical item statistics depend on the sample; IRT gives sample-invariant item and person parameters in principle and supports adaptive testing.

title: Assessing the effects of gamification in the classroom: A longitudinal study on intrinsic motivation, social comparison, satisfaction, effort, and academic performance
population: Students in two sections of one course over a semester; n not given
method_studied: Badges, leaderboard and competition in a course
finding: The gamified section showed lower intrinsic motivation, satisfaction and empowerment over time and lower performance on some measures.
notes: Sections were compared; random assignment is not stated in the record.

title: Force Concept Inventory
finding: Wrong answers diagnose a specific misconception, and instructors overestimated student understanding relative to measured scores.
effect: Interactive-engagement gains exceeded lecture gains by roughly two standard deviations in later replications, per the record
notes: The two-SD figure is attributed by the record to later replications.

title: The Four-Phase Model of Interest Development
finding: Interest moves from triggered situational to well-developed individual interest, each phase needs a different support, and interest and learning cause each other.

title: The Use of Scoring Rubrics: Reliability, Validity and Educational Consequences
population: Review of rubric studies; count not given in the record
finding: Topic-specific analytic rubrics gave higher inter-rater agreement than generic ones; benchmarks and rater training raised agreement, and some disagreement remained.

title: The Wick in the Candle of Learning
population: Participants answering trivia questions; n not given
finding: Self-rated curiosity predicted memory for the answer a week later and was tied to anticipatory activity in reward regions.
notes: The record's incidental face-memory claim closely matches the spillover claim in the Gruber 2014 record; check before citing.

title: Productive Failure
population: Eleventh grade students working in groups; n not given
finding: Students who struggled with ill-structured problems first outperformed the structured-first group on near and far transfer posttests, with worse performance during the first phase.
notes: The record says direct instruction first did better on procedural fluency.

title: The Psychology and Neuroscience of Curiosity
finding: Curiosity follows an inverted U over novelty and complexity and behaves like a drive that builds under deprivation.

title: Effectiveness of Mastery Learning Programs: A Meta-Analysis
population: 108 controlled studies of mastery learning programs
finding: Mastery programs raised exam scores by about half a standard deviation; effects were larger on researcher-made tests than standardized tests and larger in shorter studies.
effect: Mean ES = 0.52 on final exams
notes: Tier outcome. The 0.52 figure comes from the raw pass; the record says about 0.5 SD. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/sub-outcomes/education/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-46a9894f6dd8).

title: Designing the Knowledge Integration Environment
method_studied: Knowledge integration: generate, compare and reconcile ideas
finding: Prompting learners to compare and reconcile competing ideas gave more durable integration than presenting one correct idea, and integration scores predicted transfer better than a single post-test.

title: The Psychology of Curiosity: A Review and Reinterpretation
finding: Curiosity comes from a perceived gap in knowledge and peaks at intermediate uncertainty; making a gap salient raises information-seeking.
notes: Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/curiosity-and-motivation/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-e97009024405).

title: Towards Understanding the Effects of Individual Gamification Elements on Intrinsic Motivation and Performance
population: Participants on one task; n not given
method_studied: Points, levels, leaderboard and narrative as separate elements
finding: Points and levels raised task output with no significant drop in intrinsic motivation; leaderboard and narrative showed no significant change.

title: Intrinsic Motivation Systems for Autonomous Mental Development
finding: Rewarding learning progress gave faster skill acquisition than novelty or uncertainty seeking, avoiding both mastered and unlearnable regions.
notes: Robotics study; applies to learners by analogy.

title: The Effects of Choice on Intrinsic Motivation and Related Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis of Research Findings
population: 41 studies with child and adult samples
finding: Choice raised intrinsic motivation, effort, task performance and perceived competence; the effect was stronger for children and for two to four choices, and weaker when a reward followed.
notes: Record gives no pooled effect.

title: Teaching for Understanding
venue: American Educator: The Professional Journal of the American Federation of Teachers, 17(3), 8, 28-35
finding: Understanding is the ability to think and act flexibly with what one knows, shown through performances such as explaining, applying and generalizing, with stated goals and ongoing assessment.
notes: No DOI; verified against ERIC EJ473811 in the record.

title: Deep Knowledge Tracing
population: Student exercise logs from several public datasets
finding: The network beat Bayesian knowledge tracing at predicting next-answer correctness and learned skill structure without hand coding; its internal state is not interpretable.
notes: Raw pass reports a large relative AUC gain without a number.

title: Teachers as Facilitators: What Autonomy-Supportive Teachers Do and Why Their Students Benefit
finding: Autonomy-supportive behaviors can be named and trained, and students are most engaged when teachers give both autonomy support and structure.

title: Worked-Out Examples: Instructional Explanations Support Learning by Self-Explanations
population: Learners studying worked examples; n not given
method_studied: Short instructional explanations added to worked examples
finding: Short explanations raised the rate of learners' own self-explanations, and scaffolded examples beat unexplained ones on near transfer.
notes: The record's frontmatter is invalid YAML; body text was used.

title: The Power of Testing Memory: Basic Research and Implications for Educational Practice
finding: Testing gives more durable retention than equal restudy time, and the benefit grows with the retention interval.
notes: Narrative review. The raw pass holds the same authors' experiment with recall figures as a separate entry. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/memory-systems/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-0333f4a853f3).

title: Resisting Overzealous Transfer: Coordinating Previously Successful Routines With Needs for New Learning
method_studied: Coordinating old routines with new learning
finding: A routine can be applied with confidence where its assumptions fail; alternating exploration and routine practice helps learners detect when a routine needs revision.

title: Learning Trajectory Based Instruction
finding: A trajectory links a goal, a developmental path and matched tasks, is grounded in observed student reasoning, and needs ongoing formative assessment to place each student.

title: Teaching for Understanding: Linking Research with Practice
population: Teachers across subjects and grades studied over multiple years; n not given
finding: A four-part framework of generative topics, understanding goals, understanding performances and ongoing assessment; implementation quality was the strongest predictor of improvement.
notes: Book verified by ISBN in the record.

title: Reconsidering Personal Epistemology as Metacognition: A Multifaceted Approach to the Analysis of Epistemic Thinking
method_studied: Epistemic thinking as cognitive plus metacognitive
finding: Epistemic metacognition has separable parts, skills, knowledge and experiences, and instruction should target them separately.

title: Expanding the Dimensions of Epistemic Cognition: Arguments From Philosophy and Psychology
finding: Epistemic cognition has five components: aims and value, structure of knowledge, sources and justification, virtues and vices, and reliable processes; each needs context-specific analysis.
notes: Closest internal match to theory of knowledge.

title: Modeling Epistemic and Ontological Cognition: Philosophical Perspectives and Methodological Directions
finding: Integrates earlier models into four positions, realism, dogmatism, skepticism and rationalism, with justification treated as multiple means.

title: The Development of Epistemological Theories: Beliefs About Knowledge and Knowing and Their Relation to Learning
population: Review of research programs on beliefs about knowledge
method_studied: Development of epistemological beliefs and their relation to learning
finding: The programs use differing definitions and methods; the review names nine issues to resolve and frames beliefs as domain-specific and developmental.
notes: Narrative review.

title: A Developmental Model of Critical Thinking
population: Draws on research with children and adolescents
finding: Three forms of meta-knowing develop to make critical thinking possible: metacognitive, metastrategic and epistemological.

title: The development of epistemological understanding
population: Age groups from childhood through adulthood; n not given
method_studied: Levels of epistemological understanding across ages and domains
finding: Four levels, realist, absolutist, multiplist and evaluativist; understanding develops with age and the level reached differs by domain.
notes: The record states no abstract was indexed; claims were written from the paper's standard citation.

title: Views of nature of science questionnaire: Toward valid and meaningful assessment of learners' conceptions of nature of science
venue: Journal of Research in Science Teaching
population: Learners assessed for nature-of-science views; n not given
method_studied: Open-ended Views of Nature of Science questionnaire with interviews
finding: An open-ended instrument with interviews assesses nature-of-science views where forced-choice instruments fall short.

title: The curious case of climate change: Testing a theoretical model of epistemic beliefs, epistemic emotions, and complex learning
population: Students in a climate-change learning task; n not given
method_studied: Epistemic beliefs, epistemic emotions and complex learning
finding: Epistemic beliefs predicted emotions such as surprise, curiosity and confusion, which predicted outcomes on reconciling conflicting texts.
notes: The record states this is a model-testing study and was a closest-match substitute for the brief's target.

title: Understanding students' practical epistemologies and their influence on learning through inquiry
finding: Research on stated epistemological beliefs and research on inquiry practice rarely inform each other; practical epistemology governs how a student investigates.

title: Effects of Beliefs About the Nature of Knowledge on Comprehension
population: Students completing a belief questionnaire and reading passages; n not given
finding: Students who believed knowledge is simple and certain drew oversimplified conclusions; belief in quick learning predicted worse comprehension monitoring.

title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
population: Practicing designers testing guidelines; n not given
finding: Consolidates over one hundred recommendations into guidelines organized by interaction phase, several aimed at the moment the system is wrong.

title: Ironies of automation
method_studied: Automation and loss of operator skill
finding: Automating a task removes the operator's practice, so the human takes over with lost proficiency when automation fails; monitoring skill also degrades.
notes: One of the few records on skill at work. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/cognition-and-automation/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-68eb5f478fa1).

title: Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
population: Participants in AI-assisted decision tasks; n not given
method_studied: AI explanations in human-AI decision teams
finding: Team performance above both human alone and AI alone was rare; convincing explanations sometimes raised agreement with wrong AI answers.
notes: Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/sub-outcomes/education/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-4d51ec39f102).

title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
population: About 1,000 high school students in Turkey
method_studied: Unrestricted GPT-4 access versus a hints-only tutor in math practice
finding: Unrestricted access raised practice performance and lowered unassisted exam performance; the hints-only version kept the practice gain without exam harm.
effect: Unrestricted: practice +48 percent, exam -17 percent versus control. Hints only: practice +127 percent, exam -0.4 percent, not significant
notes: Sample and exact exam figure come from the raw pass. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/sub-outcomes/education/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-1b34ca6c5af4).

title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-Assisted Decision-Making
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction (CSCW)
population: Participants in AI-assisted decision tasks; n not given
finding: Forcing functions cut over-reliance on wrong AI answers more than explanations did, at a cost in speed and reported effort.

title: From Chalkboards to Chatbots: Evaluating the Impact of Generative AI on Learning Outcomes in Nigeria
venue: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper
population: Nigerian secondary students in a six-week after-school program; n not given
method_studied: GPT-4-based English tutoring with a facilitator
finding: Six weeks of structured AI tutor access produced gains described as 1.5 to 2 years of typical schooling.
effect: +0.31 SD composite; +0.23 SD English
notes: Working paper, tier candidate. The record says gains concentrated among lower performers and girls; the raw pass says gains were largest for girls and for higher initial performers. The two internal sources disagree. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/sub-outcomes/education/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-d6f23a78e535).

title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality
population: Knowledge workers in a field experiment; n not given
method_studied: AI assistance on tasks inside and outside its capability frontier
finding: AI-assisted workers outperformed controls on tasks inside the frontier and did worse on a task outside it, and could not tell which side a task was on.
notes: SSRN working paper, tier candidate. Workplace study.

title: Generative AI Enhances Individual Creativity but Reduces Collective Diversity of Novel Content
population: Writers of short stories; n not given
finding: AI-assisted stories were judged more creative individually and were more similar to each other.

title: Beware of Metacognitive Laziness: Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Learning Motivation, Processes, and Performance
population: Students with and without generative AI support; n not given
method_studied: Generative AI support during a learning task
finding: AI access reduced self-reported planning and monitoring, which mediated part of the link to lower unassisted test performance; weaker self-regulators dropped more.

title: Searching for Explanations: How the Internet Inflates Estimates of Internal Knowledge
finding: Searching in one domain raised self-rated explanatory ability on unrelated topics with no matching gain in test performance.

title: AI Tools in Society: Impacts on Cognitive Offloading and the Future of Critical Thinking
method_studied: AI-tool use, cognitive offloading and critical thinking
finding: Heavier reported AI use predicted lower critical-thinking scores, mediated by offloading; the cross-sectional self-report design cannot show cause.
notes: Tier candidate. Raw pass lists a correction, doi:10.3390/soc15090252.

title: Evaluating Explainable AI: Which Algorithmic Explanations Help Users Predict Model Behavior?
venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
population: Human subjects predicting model output; n not given
finding: Evidence that an explanation method improved a person's ability to predict model behavior appeared in few conditions; felt helpfulness did not predict measured help.

title: Principles of mixed-initiative user interfaces
venue: Proceedings of the SIGCHI conference on Human factors in computing systems the CHI is the limit - CHI '99
finding: A system should weigh the expected cost of acting or interrupting against the cost of waiting, and should let user and agent refine results together.

title: Explanation and Understanding
finding: People's explanations are incomplete in ways they do not notice, and people rely on knowledge held in other minds.

title: AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting
population: 194 college physics students in a within-class crossover
method_studied: AI tutor built on a research-based instructional design versus an active-learning class
finding: The AI-tutor group's median learning gain was more than double the classroom group's, in less time, with higher engagement.
effect: 0.63 to 1.3 SD depending on estimator; median time 49 minutes versus 60 minutes
notes: Outcome measured on the same class period's content; no delayed retention test. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/sub-outcomes/education/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-c3ad89ff9a59).

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in education
population: Survey of explainable-AI work in education
method_studied: Explainable AI for students, teachers and developers
finding: Explanation needs differ by stakeholder, and evaluation of whether an explanation improves a teacher's or student's decision is rare.

title: Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task
population: Essay writers in three conditions under EEG; n not given
method_studied: LLM-assisted versus brain-only essay writing, three conditions
finding: LLM-assisted writing showed the weakest neural connectivity, and those writers quoted their own essays less accurately.
notes: arXiv preprint, tier candidate. Assignment procedure not stated in the record. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/sub-outcomes/education/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-f3c246bffb55).

title: Effectiveness of Intelligent Tutoring Systems
population: 50 controlled evaluations of intelligent tutoring systems
method_studied: Intelligent tutoring systems versus conventional instruction
finding: Tutoring systems raised test scores; effects were larger in studies with weaker controls and held across subjects and age levels.
effect: Mean g = 0.66
notes: Tier outcome. Raw pass attributes 0.66 to the best controlled studies; the record gives it as the average across 50. Promoted to bucket-canon/07-mind/sub-outcomes/education/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-2cce3fc65496).

title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported Reductions in Cognitive Effort and Confidence Effects From a Survey of Knowledge Workers
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
population: Knowledge workers surveyed about real use examples; n not given
method_studied: Generative AI use and critical thinking at work
finding: Higher confidence in AI output went with less critical thinking, higher self-confidence with more; effort shifted toward verification and integration.
notes: Self-report survey. Workplace study.

title: The structure and function of explanations
finding: People prefer simpler and broader explanations, and explanation supports generalization to new cases.
notes: The record states no abstract was indexed.

title: Does Using Artificial Intelligence Assistance Accelerate Skill Decay and Hinder Skill Development Without Performers' Awareness?
finding: AI-assisted training is linked to faster decline in unassisted performance, and trainee confidence does not track the decay.
notes: The record states claims as findings and gives no sample; the paper's title poses a question. Treat the design as unconfirmed.

title: Spatial hypertext
finding: Arranging items by position supports early sensemaking better than typed links, which force early commitment.

title: Explanation in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Social Sciences
population: Review of philosophy and psychology literature
method_studied: Human explanation as a basis for explainable AI
finding: Most explainable-AI work rests on researcher intuition; the social sciences describe how people generate, select and evaluate explanations.
notes: Record notes the 2018 online date and 2019 print date.

title: Experimental Evidence on the Productivity Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence
finding: AI assistance cut completion time and raised output quality, with the largest gains for the lowest scorers.
notes: Workplace productivity study; measures output, with no learning measure.

title: Information foraging.
finding: People adapt search to maximize valuable information per unit cost and follow the strongest information scent.
notes: Promoted to bucket-canon/04-information/information-foraging/primary-papers.yaml (id bkt-c033b128f77f).

title: Cognitive Offloading
finding: Offloading is a cost-benefit choice that improves performance on the offloaded task; its effect on retained capacity is unresolved.

title: Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence: Reliable, Safe & Trustworthy
method_studied: Human control and automation as two dimensions
finding: High human control and high automation can coexist; full automation without oversight and full manual control are both failure modes.

title: Leveraging "Khanmigo" Generative AI-Powered Tool for Personalized Tutoring to Learn Scientific Concepts
population: Students learning physics concepts in three conditions; n not given
method_studied: Khanmigo tutoring versus web search versus paper instruction
finding: Khanmigo users scored higher than web-search users and comparable to paper-based instruction, with higher reported engagement.
notes: Tier candidate.
